pharm: Recombinant human parathyroid hormone fragment, PTH(1-34); intermittent dosing stimulates new bone formation, increasing bone mineral density and strength.
quick: Independent of food; inject thigh or abdomen
Use caution in severe impairment; no specific dose change
No specific interaction; limit for bone health
summary: Teriparatide is recombinant PTH(1-34), the first anabolic (bone-forming) osteoporosis therapy. Given as a 20 mcg subcutaneous injection once daily into the thigh or abdomen, it increases bone mass and reduces fracture risk in high-risk patients. Cumulative use should not exceed 2 years over a lifetime. Transient orthostatic hypotension can occur with early doses; supplemental calcium and vitamin D are advised.
indications: Treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture, or who have failed/are intolerant to other therapy
Increase bone mass in men with primary or hypogonadal osteoporosis at high risk for fracture
Treatment of men and women with glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (prednisone >=5 mg/day equivalent) at high risk for fracture

dosage.n: Inject into thigh or abdominal wall; rotate sites
Beyond 2 years only if patient remains/returns to high fracture risk

admin: Administer as subcutaneous injection into the thigh or abdominal wall only
Not approved for intravenous or intramuscular use
Give first doses where the patient can sit or lie down in case of orthostatic hypotension
Inspect solution; do not use if particles present or solution is discolored
Store refrigerated; discard pen 28 days after first use
moa: Acts on osteoblasts to stimulate new bone formation. Once-daily (intermittent) PTH(1-34) exposure favors bone anabolism by increasing osteoblast number and activity, improving trabecular and cortical bone microarchitecture, mass, and strength (contrasting with the catabolic effect of continuous PTH elevation).

absolute: Hypersensitivity to teriparatide or any excipient (including angioedema, anaphylaxis)
relative: Conditions with increased baseline osteosarcoma risk (Paget's disease, unexplained elevated alkaline phosphatase, prior skeletal radiation, open epiphyses in young patients)
Metabolic bone diseases other than osteoporosis
Active or recent skeletal malignancy/bone metastases

preg: Not indicated in pregnancy; used in postmenopausal women and adults with osteoporosis. Avoid use during pregnancy.
lact: Not known whether excreted in human milk; not recommended during breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution in severe renal impairment; no specific dose adjustment defined. Increased exposure may occur.

moderate: Digoxin - transient hypercalcemia may predispose to digitalis toxicity
interactions.food: May be administered without regard to meals.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; excess alcohol is detrimental to bone health.
interactions.diagnostics: Transient post-dose increases in serum calcium; measure calcium when fasting (not within hours of a dose).

rare: Osteosarcoma (seen in rat studies; rare human reports)

monitoring: Urinary calcium in patients with active or recent urolithiasis
Bone mineral density and fracture risk assessment
Orthostatic blood pressure with initial doses
counsel: Inject once daily into the thigh or stomach area; rotate injection sites
Sit or lie down for the first few doses in case you feel dizzy or lightheaded
Keep the pen refrigerated and discard 28 days after first use
Take your prescribed calcium and vitamin D
This medicine is used for a maximum of 2 years in your lifetime
Report persistent bone pain, swelling/lump, or symptoms of high calcium (nausea, constipation, excessive thirst)
pk: Serum PTH(1-34) detectable within ~30 min of SC dose
Concentrations decline within ~3 hours; daily dosing required
Refrigerate 2-8 C; use pen within 28 days of first use
pearls: First anabolic (bone-forming) agent versus antiresorptives like bisphosphonates
Most beneficial in severe osteoporosis or after failure of other agents
Antiresorptive (e.g., bisphosphonate) is usually given after stopping teriparatide to preserve gains
Rat carcinogenicity data led to historical boxed warning (since removed by FDA); avoid in patients at increased baseline osteosarcoma risk
Transient hypercalcemia peaks ~4-6 h post-dose and usually normalizes by 16-24 h
missed: If a dose is missed, inject it the same day as soon as remembered, then resume the usual schedule. Do not give two doses in one day to make up.
overdose: Effects of overdose include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and hypercalcemia. Discontinue, monitor serum calcium, hydrate, and provide supportive care; treat symptomatic hypercalcemia.
